- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add buffer below forecast or adjust downward early.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply decay or lagged smoothing to prevent overreaction.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model often lags in adjusting downward; introduce early correction if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >75% above recent 10-day average, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with historical volatility.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to smooth too much; allow 2–3% noise in forecast to capture momentum shifts.
